title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Pay Conversion and Minimum Wage Canada Comparisons
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Compare Australian minimum wage with minimum wage Canada, and understand tax, super, and casual loading
salarySummary: To convert an hourly rate to annual pay, multiply by hours per week (usually 38) and by 52 weeks, then add super on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (commonly 38 hours for full-time) and then by 52 weeks in a year. For example, $26.44 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $1004.90 per week, which gives $52,254.80 annual gross before tax. For a fortnight, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Remember that super is paid on top of this at 12% of ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Award rates are set for specific industries and occupations and are often higher. If you are covered by an award, that rate takes precedence. Always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum pay.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When converting to annual pay, include the loading in the hourly rate before multiplying by hours and weeks. Super is still calculated on the loaded rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

Whether you are negotiating a salary or comparing job offers, understanding how an hourly rate translates into annual earnings is essential. The standard formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For full-time employees in Australia, the typical working week is 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. This assumption is used in the National Minimum Wage and most award calculations.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be:

$30.00 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280.00

If you are paid fortnightly, simply double the weekly amount: $30.00 × 38 hours × 2 = $2,280.00 per fortnight before tax.

### Important Distinctions: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. This rate applies to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often provides higher minimum pay rates. Always check the relevant award using the [pay guides](/blog) or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) topic on this site.

Award rates may include penalty rates for weekends, evenings, or public holidays, and allowances for specific tasks. These are not included in the basic hourly-to-annual conversion, so your actual annual earnings could be higher if you regularly work unsocial hours.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When converting a casual rate to annual pay, apply the loading first. For instance, a casual rate of $33.05 per hour gives:

$33.05 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $65,306.80 annual gross.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your pay; your employer adds it to a super fund. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For the example above, super would be $65,306.80 × 0.12 = $7,836.82, but only up to the cap. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Comparing with Minimum Wage Canada

It can be helpful to see how Australian minimum wages compare internationally. For instance, the federal minimum wage in Canada is $18.15 per hour as of April 2026. While a direct comparison is complicated by different cost-of-living and tax systems, Australia’s National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour is significantly higher. However, many Canadian provinces set higher rates than the federal floor. When researching pay, always consider the local context. This site focuses on Australian pay, but understanding minimum wage Canada can provide perspective on global labour standards.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold and Medicare reduction thresholds are assumed based on the latest available figures. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) topic to estimate your net income.

### Average Earnings in Australia

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2083.70 per week in May 2026. For all employees (including part-time), total earnings averaged $1579.20 per week. These figures give a benchmark for typical pay. If your hourly rate converts to an annual salary near $108,352 ($2083.70 × 52), you are close to the full-time average. See [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for more details.

### Limitations of This Conversion

The formula hourly × hours per week × 52 provides a gross annual estimate. It assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a more personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/) tool on this site. You can enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading to see weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures including estimated tax and super.
